              BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA

         IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                      )
         OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY                        )
         FOR AN ORDER OF THE COMMISSION                           )
         APPROVING ITS NEW EXTRA LARGE LOAD                       )
         TARIFF AND TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF                       )     CASE NO. PUD2026-000046
         SERVICE FOR EXTRA LARGE LOAD                             )
         CUSTOMERS AND A REGULATORY ASSET TO                      )
         RECOVER COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH                            )
         PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION SOFTWARE                          )

              OG&E’S MOTION TO AMEND THE PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE IN ORDER NO.
              758969 TO INCLUDE A BRIEFING SCHEDULE REGARDING PROPOSALS FOR
                          ALTERNATIVE ELECTRIC SERVICE FRAMEWORKS

                 COMES NOW Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E” or “Company”) and

         respectfully moves the Commission to establish a briefing schedule regarding legal issues raised

         by the retail wheeling, Build-Your-Own-Generation, self-supply, or similar proposals advanced in

         Responsive Testimony filed in this proceeding and similar to issues raised in the Case No.

         PUD2025-000075 proceedings (hereinafter these proposals are referred to broadly as “Delivery

         Only Deregulated Generation Election” or “DODGE”). In support thereof, OG&E states as

         follows:

         1.      On June 17, 2026, OG&E filed its Application and Direct Testimony in this Case requesting

         the Commission approve its Extra Large Power and Light Tariff (“XLPL”), the Terms and

         Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers, and a regulatory asset to track costs

         associated with the implementation of portfolio optimization software.

         2.      In Responsive Testimony filed on September 18, 2026, the following parties proposed that

         the Commission require OG&E to offer a DODGE structure as part of the proposed XLPL Tariff.

              a. Google, LLC. See Responsive Testimony of Adrian J. Kimbrough 50:16–58:13.

              b. Oklahoma Industrial Energy Consumers.         See Responsive Testimony of James R.

                 Dauphinais 49:1–50:9.

         OG&E’s Motion to Amend Procedural Schedule                                           Page 1 of 6
         and Establish Briefing Schedule
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 45 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 6




             c. Petroleum Alliance of Oklahoma. See Responsive Testimony of David E. Dismukes 18:6–

                   19:20.

             d. Public Utility Division (“PUD”). See Responsive Testimony of David Scalf 39:18–43:17.

        3.         Further, multiple parties specifically compared OG&E’s proposed XLPL Tariff in this Case

        to a proposal—primarily made by, and in the interest of, large power users and data centers—in

        Public Service Company of Oklahoma’s pending rate case which includes a Large Load Tariff

        request, Case No. PUD2025-000075.             Notably, there was no formal legal briefing on the

        Commission’s legal authority to adopt DODGE proposals in that proceeding due to the last-minute

        nature of the surprise joint stipulation filed by Google and PUD without the support of the applicant

        utility.

        4.         Because these DODGE proposals represent a substantial departure from the XLPL tariff

        filed by OG&E and introduce numerous threshold legal questions concerning the Commission’s

        legal authority and the interaction of multiple Oklahoma statutes and regulatory frameworks, a

        focused legal briefing schedule would materially assist the Commission and promote judicial

        economy. These issues had not been raised when the existing procedural schedule was developed

        and therefore were not anticipated or accommodated in Order No. 758969. 1

        5.         Parties to this case have a material legal dispute regarding:

             a. Whether Oklahoma law authorizes the Commission to approve DODGE frameworks;

             b. Whether such proposals violate the Retail Electric Supplier Certified Territory Act;

             c. Whether such proposals are consistent with Oklahoma’s statutory limitations on retail

                   electric competition;

             d. Whether such proposals would permit or facilitate retail wheeling;


        1
          Parties to this Case communicated a negotiated procedural schedule to the ALJ on June 24, 2026 and was
        recommended by the ALJ on June 25, 2026. DODGE frameworks were proposed by parties to the separate PUD2025-
        000075 for the first time on June 26, 20206.

        and Establish Briefing Schedule
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 45 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 6




             e. Whether proposed arrangements improperly rely upon unauthorized/unregulated retail

                electric service under the guise of “wholesale-market” transactions;

             f. Whether such proposals are consistent with the obligations imposed upon regulated public

                utilities;

             g. Whether such proposals are consistent with House Bill 2992 and related provisions of Title

                17; and,

             h. Whether such proposals relieve the utility of any legal obligation to serve the bypassing

                customer.

        6.      Resolution of these legal questions will materially affect the manner in which evidence is

        presented and evaluated during the merits hearing. Focused legal briefing will therefore aid both

        the parties and the Commission by identifying the precise legal authority allegedly supporting the

        proposals and narrowing issues that require development.

        7.      Good cause exists to establish a briefing schedule because:

                a. The DODGE proposals raised in Responsive Testimony present substantial questions

                    of law;

                b. Resolution of those issues will streamline the hearing;

                c. The issues affect the scope of admissible evidence and testimony;

                d. Separate briefing will promote judicial economy and will prevent surprise and ensure

                    procedural fairness; and

                e. The Commission will benefit from focused advocacy directed specifically to the legal

                    issues presented that need to be decided in this matter.

        8.      The Commission’s Procedural Order, Order No. 758969, expressly provides that “[a]ll pre-

        trial disputes, matters and/or issues shall be brought before the ALJ” and further designates the

        ALJ to preside over all pretrial matters in this proceeding.

        OG&E’s Motion to Amend Procedural Schedule                                            Page 3 of 6
        and Establish Briefing Schedule

        9.       To facilitate the development of a full and complete record, OG&E believes the procedural

        schedule should be amended to provide for a meaningful opportunity to brief the threshold legal

        and jurisdictional issues raised by the DODGE proposals before proceeding to the merits hearing.

        Such briefing will ensure that the Commission’s consideration of those proposals is informed by a

        clearly developed legal record and will assist the parties in presenting evidence responsive to the

        Commission’s resolution of those issues.

        10.       OG&E respectfully proposes the following amended scheduling dates to address the legal

        issues injected into these proceedings by intervenors through Responsive Testimony:

             Settlement Conference [no change]            October 16, 2026

             [modified]

             of Law [modified]


                                              REQUESTED RELIEF

        11.       The DODGE frameworks advanced in Responsive Testimony present significant threshold

        legal and jurisdictional issues that are distinct from ordinary ratemaking questions and warrant a

        OG&E’s Motion to Amend Procedural Schedule                                             Page 4 of 6
        and Establish Briefing Schedule

        specific legal briefing schedule included within the schedule for processing this Case. A slight

        delay in hearing-related dates to accommodate a formal briefing schedule will promote fairness,

        efficiency, and the development of a clear record for the Commission’s consideration of specific

        legal issues.

        12.     WHEREFORE, OG&E respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judge establish,

        or alternatively recommend that the Commission establish, a formal legal briefing schedule and

        modify the scheduling dates currently set forth in Order No. 758969 as set forth herein regarding

        any DODGE or similar proposed service structure and grant such other and further relief as may

        be just and proper.
